targets.title: Analytic thinking promotes religious disbelief.
targets.evidence_quote: First, we sought a direct replication of the finding that individual differences in analytic thinking are negatively related to religious beliefs when the two constructs are measured in the typical order (i.e., analytic thinking assessed first) [ 8 ].
targets.outcome_quote: We replicated the negative relationship between analytic thinking and religious beliefs as reported by Gervais and Norenzayan (Study 1) [ 8 ], but only when analytic thinking was measured first. Reversing the measurement order reduced the relationship to non-significance.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Close replication succeeds; changing measurement order removes the relationship. The paper explicitly frames the target relationship as conditional, with agreement in one condition and disagreement in the other.

targets.authors: Pennycook G, Cheyne JA, Barr N, Koehler DJ, Fugelsang JA.
targets.title: Cognitive style and religiosity: The role of conflict detection.
targets.evidence_quote: Furthermore, in light of prior evidence linking the need for cognition (NFC) and religiosity [ 11 ], we also included a measure of need for cognition (NFC) at the end of the study to allow for exploratory analyses probing the relationship between NFC and religious beliefs; these analyses yielded additional support for the measurement order hypothesis.
targets.outcome_quote: These patterns mirror findings reported by Pennycook et al. (Study 1) [ 11 ]. When participants completed the religious beliefs measures first, however, NFC was no longer correlated with any of the religious beliefs measures: intrinsic religiosity r (205) = .06, p = .394; intuitive religious beliefs r (205) = .06, p = .384; belief in supernatural agents r (205) = .03, p = .647.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Explicit exploratory re-test of NFC/religiosity relationship agrees under analytic-first order and fails under reversed order. The reference prints 2013 (despite volume issue metadata suggesting a later issue).

reasoning: Title and three authors verified. Independent sample tests the published analytic-thinking relationship and additionally the NFC relationship. Shenhav, other Pennycook papers and Gervais (2015) are discussed as contextual comparisons; this paper does not designate their distinct studies as targets. Measurement-order comparisons yield mixed outcomes. The mechanism critique proposes priming as an explanation but the observed conditional relationship is the substantive verdict.
